name: Velora
summary: Unified operations platform for nonprofits: Keela (donor CRM), Aplos (fund accounting) and Raisely (online fundraising) as one connected suite — donor management, campaigns and finances built for charities instead of adapted from business software.
best_for: nonprofits that want donor CRM, fund accounting and online fundraising from one vendor, purpose-built for charities rather than adapted business tools
skip_if: you're a tiny charity that only needs a donation page (free tools cover that), or you're deeply invested in one best-of-breed piece already
honest_knock: Velora is three acquired products (Keela, Aplos, Raisely) being unified into one platform, and that's the honest watch-out: integration between them is newer than the marketing suggests, so check how deeply the pieces actually connect for your workflow before committing. Costs also stack per product and per contact count — a growing donor base raises the CRM bill. For nonprofits though, purpose-built beats adapted business software in fund accounting specifically.

pricing.notes: Quote-only. joinvelora.com (read in a browser on 5 September 2026) has no pricing page and no amount anywhere; every call to action is 'Talk to sales'. Velora bundles Keela (CRM), Aplos (accounting) and Raisely (fundraising) for nonprofits, and the individual product prices are not shown on the unified site. The products' own pricing pages still publish them — read 25 September 2026, Keela from $164 a month billed annually ($190 monthly) for up to 1,000 contacts, Aplos Lite at $79 a month, and Raisely with no monthly fee — but whether a Velora contract uses those rates is something only sales can confirm. Our earlier note of Keela 'from about $134' is out of date.

cost_traps.label: Quote-only pricing
cost_traps.evidence: No pricing page or amount for the bundled product itself; every call to action is 'Talk to sales' (read 5 Sep 2026)

compare_with.name: Blackbaud or Bloomerang plus QuickBooks
compare_with.why: the legacy giant vs a DIY stack — Velora sits between: integrated and nonprofit-native without Blackbaud's enterprise weight

open_questions.question: Can you publish a price, or a starting price, for the plans that are quote-only?
Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?
